insight:
The map shows how suitable each province is for geothermal energy. The average score is 14.5 out of a possible 38, and every province has a value. Most provinces fall into the “very low” group (84), while 34 are labeled “low.” Even places that sit close to active volcanoes or existing geothermal power plants often score only low, not high.

For example, Biliran scores the highest at 38.15 but is still classified as low. It sits just 9.9 km from the Biliran volcano and 11.4 km from a 2 MW operating plant. Pampanga (36.09) is 33 km from Mount Pinatubo, and Batangas (34.35) is within 14 km of Taal volcano and near two operating plants (20 MW and 63 MW). The reason the scores do not jump to high is that surface volcanism is only one piece of the puzzle. A usable geothermal resource also needs a hot rock reservoir that can let water flow through it (permeability) and terrain that can be reached for drilling. If the underground rocks are cool, sealed, or hard to access, the potential stays low even though a volcano is nearby.

Sources: municipalities table, provinces table, geothermal_suitability table, fastapi-backend/app/services/geothermal/plants.py, fastapi-backend/app/services/local_data/geothermal_volcanoes.json, GeothermalDatasets/philippine_volcanoes.csv
